h: Mustard, Canaries and a cheeky hole-in-one
p: Norwich has a habit of surprising first-time visitors. It's the home of Colman's mustard, it's got a football club nicknamed the Canaries who play at Carrow Road, and its tangle of lanes is packed with independent shops. So a round of crazy golf fits right into a day of poking about and finding odd little gems.

On the practical side, a round usually takes around an hour, a bit more with a big crowd. Pick a scorekeeper before you start, agree a sensible cap on shots per hole so nobody is stuck on the windmill equivalent for twenty minutes, and keep the phones handy for the inevitable slow-motion replay of someone's spectacular miss.

For more to fill the day, the Norwich Lanes area around St Benedict's Street and Pottergate is great for browsing, and The Forum, the big glass building by the market, often has free events and exhibitions going on inside. Tombland, by the cathedral gates, is one of the oldest parts of the city, and a riverside walk takes you past Pull's Ferry, the old flint watergate on the Wensum. Strangers' Hall, a historic merchant's house museum, gives a peek at how Norwich folk lived centuries ago.

Out on the edge of the city, the Sainsbury Centre at the University of East Anglia is an art gallery in a striking building, and it's free to wander the campus and its lake. If you've got a whole weekend, the trains run out to the coast at Cromer and Great Yarmouth, so you could swap your putter for a bucket and spade the next day.
